title: TCD-016-C1 Model-Evolution Evidence Acquisition and Rewetting Validation

internal_evidence_exhaustion.conclusion: Frozen ANIMO source, user-guide evidence and SQ02-SQ09 do not identify the continuation material strongly enough to select a physical rewetting law.

search_questions: Is there authoritative evidence that an unidentified dry NH4-N surface residue can universally be treated as fully and instantaneously rewettable into surface aqueous NH4?
Is there evidence that plausible ammonium-bearing dry phases can rehydrate or dissolve on water return?
Are there credible competing fates that prevent complete instantaneous remobilization from being a universal constitutive law?
Is there process-specific validation sufficiently close to the ANIMO TCD-016 control-volume problem to discriminate complete, partial, delayed or alternative-receiver behavior?

bounded_search_protocol.method: targeted scholarly web search of publisher and scholarly-index pages
query_families: ammonium dry residue rewetting dissolution surface water fertilizer experiment
ammonium fixation drying rewetting clay soil
ammonia volatilization ammonium solution surface review
ammonium sulfate deliquescence water uptake laboratory
bounded_search_protocol.admissibility_rule: A paper can support the SQ09 candidate only if its material identity, control volume, activation condition, receiver and transfer behavior can be mapped traceably to M_surface_NH4_non_aqueous_continuation. Generic ammonium chemistry is supporting or counter evidence only.
bounded_search_protocol.absence_claim_limit: NO_QUALIFYING_EVIDENCE_FOUND_IN_THIS_BOUNDED_SEARCH; this is not a claim that no such evidence exists anywhere.

sources.citation: Nieder, R., Benbi, D.K. & Scherer, H.W. (2011). Fixation and defixation of ammonium in soils: a review. Biology and Fertility of Soils 47, 1-14.
sources.relevance: Documents rapid and strongly soil/mineral-dependent NH4 fixation and variable defixation/availability, including moisture dependence.
sources.reason_not_qualifying: The ANIMO continuation state is not identified as clay-fixed NH4, and the source does not validate the SQ09 surface-residue receiver or kinetics.

sources.citation: Opuwariboi, E. & Odu, C.T.I. (1975). Fixed ammonium in Nigerian soils III. Capacity of organic and inorganic soil components to retain added ammonium. Journal of Soil Science 26, 358-363.
sources.relevance: Reports substantial retained ammonium after repeated wetting and drying, demonstrating that wet-dry cycling need not imply complete immediate aqueous recovery.
sources.reason_not_qualifying: The experimental matrix is soil and does not identify the ANIMO surface continuation material.

sources.citation: Montes, F., Rotz, C.A. & Chaoui, H. (2009). Process Modeling of Ammonia Volatilization from Ammonium Solution and Manure Surfaces: A Review with Recommended Models. Transactions of the ASABE 52(5), 1707-1720.
sources.relevance: Shows ammonia loss from ammonium-containing surfaces depends on temperature, pH, ionic strength and air-flow mass transfer, with laboratory validation for buffered ammonium-water solutions and manure.
sources.reason_not_qualifying: It constrains NH3/NH4 aqueous-surface volatilization but does not establish the dry continuation material or complete instantaneous redissolution.

sources.citation: Bouwman, A.F. et al. (2002). Estimation of global NH3 volatilization loss from synthetic fertilizers and animal manure applied to arable lands and grasslands. Global Biogeochemical Cycles 16.
sources.relevance: Shows ammoniacal N fate is controlled by multiple interacting factors including pH, CEC, temperature, water and fertilizer form; NH4 can be retained, nitrified or converted to volatile NH3.
sources.reason_not_qualifying: The synthesis does not identify the TCD-016 continuation phase and cannot choose its receiver/kinetics.

sources.citation: Brooks, S.D. et al. (2002). Deliquescence behavior of organic/ammonium sulfate aerosol. Geophysical Research Letters 29.
sources.relevance: Shows a known ammonium-sulfate phase is highly water-soluble and exhibits phase-specific deliquescence behavior.
sources.reason_not_qualifying: SQ08 did not identify the continuation mass as ammonium sulfate or any other specific salt; phase-specific deliquescence cannot be transferred to an unidentified state.

positive_support: Known ammonium salts can be strongly water-soluble and can deliquesce under phase-specific conditions.
A rewettable-residue model is chemically plausible for some material identities.
counterevidence_and_alternatives: NH4 can become fixed or otherwise retained by mineral or soil matrices and later defix at variable rates.
Ammoniacal N can partition toward NH3 volatilization depending on pH, temperature, ionic strength, airflow and water regime.
Wetting and drying does not imply one universal receiver or instantaneous complete remobilization.
evidence_synthesis.critical_mapping_gap: No source maps M_surface_NH4_non_aqueous_continuation to a specific material class for which complete instantaneous transfer to SURFACE_AQUEOUS_NH4_STORAGE is established.
evidence_synthesis.process_validation_gap: No located source reproduces or closely analogizes the exact ANIMO sequence of ponded surface NH4, dry-down to zero explicit aqueous storage, retained continuation mass, and quantified rewetting receiver/time course.

minimum_observables: initial dissolved surface NH4-N mass before dry-down
retained total NH4-N after dry-down with atmospheric loss separately quantified or bounded
material or phase characterization sufficient to map the retained pool
soil/mineral receiver NH4-N where contact is possible
gaseous NH3-N during dry-down and rewetting where relevant
mass closure across aqueous, retained/fixed, soil/mineral and gaseous terms
